title: Review of c41's CIPS parasite negative on fresh seed 2: at the slow kinetics the parasite again condenses inside every body (14-15 spots on 14-16 bodies), shrinks them and slows division (16 -> 15 bodies vs 16 -> 17-19 in the c-free twin), with no free-living predator; Supported
summary: I ran the finding's world_base.py with labkit on seed 2 (t=8000: 14 bodies, 6 persistent splits, 0 merges) and the finding's pred.py on seed 2: checkpoint at t=8000, then the paired arms with the finding's slow kinetics (kp 0.02, kd 0.003, Dc 0.05, chic 3, order 1, noise c0 0.02) and the c-free twin (kp 0), 7500 t each (arms/). Parasite arm: within 450 t one c spot forms per body (15 spots on 15 bodies; 14-15 for the rest of the run), total c settles at ~1050, prey bodies 16 -> 14-15 to t=15200, the bodies shrink (arms/pred_s2_pred.png) and divide little. Twin: c decays away by t~11000, prey 16 -> 19 (t=11150-12050) -> 17. No c spot exists outside a body and there are no oscillations: the parasite is a passenger, as the finding says.

observations.X: arms/s2_pred.log vs arms/s2_twin.log: prey 16 -> 15 with c inside 14-15 bodies vs 16 -> 17 (max 19) in the c-free twin; arms/pred_s2_pred.png: c only inside bodies, none free

seeds_run.result: pass: endosymbiont-like c in every body, fewer prey than the twin (15 vs 17 at the end), no free predators

controls_run.X: arms/s2_twin.log (kp=0 c-free twin from the same t=8000 checkpoint)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed, slow-kinetics arm only; I did not re-run the fast-kinetics screens (all-or-nothing outcome). The prey difference is small (15 vs 17 bodies) and the twin itself fluctuates (19 -> 17).
